title: Compass snapshot: goal deltas + weekly coda
content:
Quick snapshot (one paragraph):
I want a short, scannable memo I can read in <2m each Friday. This is the compass snapshot for my personal goals: what moved, what stalled, the riskiest assumption, and one tiny experiment to run next week. Notes are intentionally choppy.

This week's headline: slow steady progress on Focus Hours, but hands-off automation experiment (auto-priority rules) ate 2 days of context switching on Tuesday. Learned: set guardrails before handing off.

Metrics (weekly window; target = weekly goal):
- Focus hours (blocked, deep work): 14 / 20 target (baseline 9) -> +5 vs last week
- PRs merged (feature + infra): 3 / 4 target -> -1 (blocked by infra test flakiness)
- Meetings (total): 7.5h (goal <= 6h) -> -1.5h over target; need to trim recurring syncs
- Learning (reading + docs): 3.5h (goal 4h) -> on track
- Mental bandwidth score (end-of-day quick rating): 6.2/10 (target >=7) -> friction from context switching

OKR alignment (current quarter):
- Objective: Reduce tail latency and reduce iteration cost for serving runtime.
  - Key result 1: Reduce p95 inference latency on medium-length prompts by 10% (current +4%)
  - Key result 2: Cut CI->deploy iteration time by 20% (current +7%)
  - How I map this week: focused on a small SLO alert refactor and wrote the deploy playbook draft.

What moved (wins):
- Wrote first draft of deploy playbook and handoff checklist; should reduce noisy pages during deploys.
- Experimented with calendar batching (2x blocks) and got one 3-hour deep block. Felt productive.
- Resolved flaky e2e test in feature-X by adding deterministic seed; unblocks PRs.

What stalled / blockers:
- Autoscheduler rules I handed off caused frequent escalations (ops ping at 9am-11am Tue/Wed). Need pre-launch checklist for rule changes.
- Did not get to the quantization recommendation doc for Optimize; deprioritized because of infra incidents.

Hypotheses to test (next week):
1) If I add a short checklist (3 items) before flipping autoscheduler rules, ops interruptions will drop by 60%.
- Measurement: # of pages tagged "autoscheduler" and duration of followups.
2) If I keep calendar batching to 3 blocks/wk, deep-focus hours will average >=16.
- Measurement: Focus hours + subjective bandwidth score.

Tiny experiment plan (one-sentence):
- Implement a 3-item autoscheduler preflight slack modal (owner, rollback, test-case) and soft-enforce it for 1 week; record incidents.

Commitments for next week (specific & small):
- Ship deploy playbook v0.2 and ask Devin for playthrough by Tue.
- Add preflight modal and alert rule to staging by Wed EOD.
- Trim 30m from two recurring syncs (ask to reduce cadence) by Thu.
- Reserve two 3-hour deep blocks on calendar (Mon, Thu).

Open questions / notes to self (scratch):
- Is the deep-work metric too blunt? Maybe track 'uninterrupted deep focus' (>=60m) vs aggregated short blocks.
- Should I track context switches (number of app switches per day)? Might help correlate with bandwidth score.
- Who else on team treats autoscheduler as product-level change? Flag for process doc.

Quick log (raw timeline, mins):
- Mon: triage + 90m deep (playbook outline), 60m meetings (kickoff + sync)
- Tue: context-switching day, 120m lost to ops pings, 30m deep (fix e2e)
- Wed: 150m deep (deploy checklist + PR reviews), 90m meetings
- Thu: 180m deep (calendar batching success), 30m docs
- Fri: 60m learning (paper), 45m planning

Retro (short):
- Keep doing: calendar batching, small deploy playbook drafts before deploy.
- Stop doing: handing off rule flips without a checklist.
- Try: 'preflight modal' + track incidents for 2 weeks.

Artifacts to link when I flesh this out:
- Confluence playbook draft link -> COMPASS-OKR-2025-2 (linked above)
- Example autoscheduler PR -> github.com/redwood-inference/internal-notes/pull/218
- Incident timeline JIRA -> JIRA-TEAM-1147

Next review cadence: quick scan every Friday morning (2m), deeper edit once per sprint (Wed mid-sprint).

Notes to self (end):
- If this grows noisy, move the playbook out of personal doc into product/console folder and create a GH issue for followups.
- Keep this doc intentionally short; if it's > 800 words it's doing too much.

----
Version history (short):
- 2025-08-12: initial template and first entries.
- 2025-11-19: started tracking Focus Hours explicitly.
- 2026-02-25: added 'preflight modal' experiment hypothesis.
_warnings: All values are strings or lists; content is freeform text with line breaks.
